# Dimensions

Source: [`Kernel/Dimensions.wl`](../../Kernel/Dimensions.wl) · Design notes: [MODULES.md](../MODULES.md#dimensions-kerneldimensionswl--derivedimensions)

DeriveDimensions: the scaling dimension of every coupling, field and of time, derived from the ansatz under the assumption that Gamma\_k = Integral dt d^dx density has no dimension, and written in a basis chosen by the user: the RG scale k and N+1 reference couplings. Objective, assumptions and checks: docs/MODULES.md section "Dimensions".

## Symbols

### `DeriveDimensions`

`DeriveDimensions[ansatz, "References" -> {nk -> "nu", Dhk -> "h", Dphik -> "phi"}, "Dimensionless" -> {Ak, ...}]` derives the dimension of every coupling, field and of time as k^x ref1^y1 ... ref\_{N+1}^y\_{N+1} (N+1 references, N = number of scalars) and returns the "Dimensions" stage. A reference may be written nk -> {"nu", "Mode" -> "Running"} or nk -> {"nu", "Mode" -> "Running", "Equation" -> nk ank} (see AdimensionalEquations). Options: "Names" -> &lt;\|gk -> ghat\|> (dimensionless names), "Scale" -> k.

### `ShowDimensions`

`ShowDimensions[dims]` prints the dimension table: coupling \| monomials it appears in \| dimension \| dimensionless name \| linear part of its flow; then the fields, time and the frequency exponent z.

### `CheckDimensions`

`CheckDimensions[dims, <|gk -> k Dphik^(1/2) Dhk^(-1/2) nk, H -> ..., "Frequency" -> k^2 nk|>]` compares hand-derived dimensions with the derived ones exactly; any mismatch prints a FAIL block and aborts. Returns the list of compared keys.

### `DimensionOf`

`DimensionOf[dims, x]` is the dimension of the coupling or field x (or "Frequency", "Time") as k^x ref^y.

### `LinearPart`

`LinearPart[dims, c]` is the canonical part of the flow of the dimensionless coupling: -x + Sum\_j y\_j eta\_j for c of dimension k^x Prod\_j ref\_j^y\_j, so that d\_s chat = chat LinearPart + (d\_s c)/\[c\] (d\_s ref\_j = -eta\_j ref\_j).

### `AnsatzOf`

`AnsatzOf[stage]` returns the Ansatz stage embedded in a later stage (e.g. an Equations stage read by LoadStage).

### `EmbeddedStage`

`EmbeddedStage[stage, name]` returns the stage called name embedded (at any depth) in stage, or Missing.
